question.text: A USDINR call option has delta = 0.55. Current premium is Rs. 0.45. If USDINR moves from 82.80 to 83.10, what is the expected new premium?

explanation.text: The Logic: Delta measures the expected change in option premium for a one-unit change in the underlying. Change in premium = 0.55 x (83.10 - 82.80) = 0.55 x 0.30 = 0.165. New premium = 0.45 + 0.165 = Rs. 0.615, matching the USDINR delta example in the workbook. The Trap: Multiplying delta by the current premium ignores how delta is defined; delta scales movement in the underlying, not the premium itself. Because of gamma, the delta-based estimate is only directionally accurate for small moves in the underlying. Note: Workbook reference — pp.73-74 (delta formula and matching USDINR delta example).
